content.text: Errors begin at the start of the abnormal window and are total for `/hotels` and `/recommendations`. Next I'll break frontend's HTTP routes down by status in both periods to see which user paths are affected.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, span_name, attr_http_response_status_code code, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(duration)/1e6,2) ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', span_name, attr_http_response_status_code, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(duration)/1e6,2) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.text: Frontend's `/hotels` and `/recommendations` routes fail completely, while `/cinema`, `/museums` and `/reservation` are fine. I still need to decide what kind of fault rate is. I'll compare the rate and memcached-rate metrics across periods and look at logs from rate and search.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(value),4) avg_v, ROUND(MAX(value),4) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE (service_name IN ('rate','memcached-rate-1','search') OR attr_k8s_deployment_name='rate') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.pod.network.io.receive','k8s.pod.network.io.transmit','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(value),4), ROUND(MAX(value),4) FROM normal_metrics WHERE (service_name IN ('rate','memcached-rate-1','search') OR attr_k8s_deployment_name='rate') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.pod.network.io.receive','k8s.pod.network.io.transmit','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,4,1
SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, level, COUNT(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, COUNT(*) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.text: Rate's CPU dropped from about 0.0062 to 0.0008 while its pod stayed up. That points to requests never reaching it, rather than rate itself saturating. I'll look at the duration distribution of search's failed rate calls to tell a timeout from a fast refusal.

Reservation CheckAvailability drop (921->0) is downstream of /hotels failing, not a fault. Restarts flat. Kinds: profile=pod_unavailable; rate=dns_lookup_failed (fast failure without connection, pod healthy, no hubble metrics to show network). Propagation: profile->frontend, rate->search, search->frontend.
